sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_medications: Amlodipine 5mg PO daily x90d; Levetiracetam 500mg PO BID x30d
sections.follow_up: Neurology/neurosurgery follow-up within 2-4 weeks. Repeat imaging per plan.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 60/100 → moderate assistance (Feeding 5, Bathing 5, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: Nursing problem: risk for raised intracranial pressure and altered neurological status. Goal: BP stays within the ordered range and neurological status does not worsen. Observation: Observe consciousness, pupils, weakness, headache and vomiting frequently and check BP; Assess swallowing. Care: Keep ordered BP control and bed rest with the head raised; Take fall precautions, reposition to prevent contracture and coordinate early rehabilitation. Education: Ask the patient to report headache, nausea or weakness at once.
sections.nursing_diagnosis: Nursing diagnoses: risk for raised intracranial pressure and altered neurological status, risk for falls / injury, risk for impaired swallowing, self-care deficit.
sections.nursing_history: Admission reason: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness. PMH: Hypertension (HTN), Atrial fibrillation (AF).
sections.risk_assessments: Fall / pressure ulcer risk: assessment pending

sections.admission_status: Hospital stay: 12 days. Admission reason: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness. Fever had not resolved; discharged with outpatient follow-up arranged.
sections.nursing_interventions_provided: Medication administration: 101 doses (4 drugs); Vital-sign monitoring: 180 sets; Oxygen therapy: observed on 156 sets of vital signs; Procedures: Urinary catheter insertion, Nasogastric tube insertion, Transthoracic echocardiography, Central venous catheter insertion, Craniotomy for intracranial hematoma evacuation; Cumulative IN 13524 mL / OUT 13183 mL (net +341 mL); Education: Ask the patient to report headache, nausea or weakness at once.
sections.patient_education: Patient education: BP control, salt restriction and medication adherence; recurrence signs and when to call for help; continuing rehabilitation and home safety.

sections.op_procedure_name: Procedure: Craniectomy or craniotomy for evacuation of hematoma, supratentorial; intracerebral (code 61313); operative time 160 min

sections.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness
sections.ed_workup: Labs: PT-INR 1.0, APTT 29.6 s, fibrinogen 383.0 mg/dL, creatinine 0.84 mg/dL, BUN 17.3 mg/dL, Na 139.0 mmol/L, K 4.2 mmol/L, glucose 119.0 mg/dL [H]. Imaging: head CT (without contrast) (Acute right basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with mass effect). Medications: Nicardipine, Labetalol
sections.physical_exam: On arrival: BP 131/74 mmHg, HR 96 bpm, RR 18 /min, SpO2 94%, T 36.3°C. General: drowsy, responds to voice, acutely ill-appearing, in marked distress. Neurological: dense left hemiplegia (MMT 0-1/5), left facial palsy, dysarthria, left hemispatial neglect, forced gaze deviation to the right; NIHSS 24.
sections.triage_details: Triage level: ESI Level 2. Arrival mode: Ambulance. Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).
